findings.evidence: Line 241 vs. lines 46-49 ("The schemes rescaling a merged pair ... the set is what lets them meet the criterion"); lines 176-177, 198-200 and 382-385 all quantify over `{R : RecombinationScheme V}`.
findings.fix: Restrict the claim to the `eScheme`-specific results, e.g. "does not satisfy the lemmas proved for `eScheme` below", or delete the clause.
findings.issue: `eScheme` docstring claims a masslessness-restoring scheme "inherits none of the theorems proved here". False: `isLinearMap_uncurry_iff`, `IsPosHomogeneous.isCollinearExactOn_iff` and `IsCollinearExact.isCollinearSafe_iff` are stated for an arbitrary `R : RecombinationScheme V`. It also contradicts the module docstring (lines 46-49), which says exactly such a scheme meets the `isCollinearExactOn_iff` criterion proved in this file.

findings.evidence: Grep for `Recombination.lean` shows `massless` at lines 22, 46, 48, 127, 195-197, 239-241; no `p`-scheme, `E₀`-scheme, `Frame` or mass structure occurs in the file, and its `variable` lines (112, 265, 320, 374) assume only `AddCommGroup`/`Module ℝ`.
findings.fix: State the criterion abstractly (a set on which the rescaling factor is trivial / closed under positive rescaling). If the `p`-scheme motivation is kept, keep it once in the module docstring, flagged as motivation for a scheme not yet defined and naming the bilinear form that makes "massless" meaningful.
findings.issue: Four docstrings assert, as established fact, properties of frame-rescaling schemes that are not defined in the repository, and speak of "massless momenta" although `V` here carries only `[AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V]` — no metric, so masslessness is undefined (`Basic.lean` defines mass only relative to a chosen `LinearMap.BilinForm`). Same problem at lines 46-49 (module), 195-197 (`IsPosHomogeneous.isCollinearExactOn_iff`), 239-241 (`eScheme`). A reader cannot check "can only have this for a set of massless momenta" or "meets it on the massless momenta" against anything in the library.

findings.evidence: Line 353: `theorem not_isCollinearExact_smulScheme [Nontrivial V] {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 1)`; line 336 `smulScheme_one : smulScheme V 1 = eScheme V`.
findings.fix: Add "on a nontrivial `V`" in both places, and "for `c ≠ 1`" in the module docstring.
findings.issue: `smulScheme`'s docstring says "For `c ≠ 1` it is additive, positively homogeneous of degree one and symmetric and still not collinear exact", omitting the `[Nontrivial V]` hypothesis that `not_isCollinearExact_smulScheme` requires; on a trivial `V` the scheme is exact. The module docstring (lines 39-41) is worse: it says `smulScheme` "has all three and merges a collinear pair into `c • p` (`not_isCollinearExact_smulScheme`)" with neither `c ≠ 1` nor nontriviality.

findings.evidence: Lines 364-366 `not_isUnital_smulScheme ... {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 1)` holds for every `c ≠ 1`, including `c < 1`.
findings.fix: Replace with a direction-neutral statement: a non-unital scheme changes a pseudojet's momentum when an infinitely soft particle is merged into it.
findings.issue: `IsUnital` docstring concludes "so a scheme that is not unital manufactures momentum out of an infinitely soft particle". A non-unital scheme can equally destroy momentum — the file's own `not_isUnital_smulScheme` applies to `c = 1/2`, which halves it.

findings.evidence: Grep shows `clustering`/`distance measure` in `EpsilonEridani/QFT/Jets/` occur only in this file's prose; `Basic.lean:158` defines `IsCollinearSafe (O : Multiset V → X)` as an observable predicate, and no `Clustering` declaration exists.
findings.fix: Call `J` an observable, matching `Basic.lean`, and drop the appeals to an undefined distance measure from the declaration docstrings (one sentence of motivation in the module docstring is enough).
findings.issue: `IsCollinearExact.isCollinearSafe_iff` and `IsUnital.tendsto_cons` (line 396) describe `J : Multiset V → X` as a "clustering" and justify their hypotheses by what "a distance measure vanishing on collinear pairs" delivers; neither notion exists in the repository, and `IsCollinearSafe` is `Basic.lean`'s predicate on observables, with `J` here an arbitrary function.

summary: The module docstring and most declaration docstrings are substantive and accurate, but several overclaim: `eScheme`'s docstring contradicts the module docstring about what a rescaling scheme inherits, four docstrings assert unproven properties of `p`/`E₀`-type schemes and of "masslessness" that has no meaning for this file's `V`, and the `smulScheme` and `IsUnital` docstrings state consequences the file's own theorems do not support.
